reason: The schedule is fine but the rule as written is broken. SCHEDULE: a scored probe before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC is easy (P ~0.9). The build takes 15 min, one ~40 min T4 dummy run fits after the 26 Sep 00:00 UTC reset, a submit around 01:00-03:00 UTC gets scored around 09:00-14:00 UTC on 26 Sep, and that leaves ~70 h of buffer. IMPLEMENTATION AS DESCRIBED: 'degrade if elapsed + remaining x (1.3 x p90 repair_s) > 11 h' is all-or-nothing, because the estimate covers the WHOLE remaining tail. When the full tail cannot fit, the rule switches off relink/gap/safe-div/linefit for everything after the first few datasets. So it repairs FEWER datasets than the author's fixed 7.5 h guard. In a simulation (110 datasets, lognormal repair times; G = end of the GPU phase, R = full repair loop) the fraction fully repaired was, for the original / the idea / a fixed 10 h deadline: G=6.5 h, R=2.5 h -> 0.43/0.07/1.00; G=6 h, R=4 h -> 0.40/0.03/1.00; G=7 h, R=2.5 h -> 0.23/0.06/1.00 (scratchpad sim.py, notes). This failure sits inside the idea's own scenario range (T=8-8.5 h, R=1.5-2.5 h, so G=6-6.5 h). The 4-clip dummy runs can never exercise it, so only a public drop would catch it, and that costs a slot. Verified facts: REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=27000 is an env var set in x138 code cell 0 l.74; cell 5 l.2116 checks at each dataset start and the flag is sticky; the geffs are sorted (l.2072); the repair loop runs after all prediction, and write_test_submission is called once because the validator is off. divinsert is not gated (build_probe_kernel.py l.302: frame reads + DaughterNet per dataset), so exp57b crosses 27000 s sooner, and #35 vs #34 may be confounded by the guard itself. Latencies of our comparable stacks: 7.0-7.2 h (#29/#30), 7.5 h (#28, #31), ~7.8 h (#32/#33). Dummy runtime varies 1.5x between runs of the same compute (exp51 29 min vs exp52 43 min, RESULTS.md l.64-66). No exp56 hidden-run or dummy logs exist in the repo, so the GPU/repair split is unknown.
fix_if_any: Drop the projection rule. Build tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 [--patch divinsert --set DIVINS_ENABLE=1 ... as in exp57b] --set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=34200 (9.5 h). This needs ZERO new code: --set on x138 appends os.environ lines at the end of cell 0 after l.74, and cell 5 reads the env var. It dominates the author's 7.5 h guard in every simulated case and finishes by <= ~10.3-11 h. Safety check before choosing 34200 vs 36000: from the exp56/exp57b dummy log (kaggle kernels output, or the browser) take the per-dataset 'FINAL ... | Xs' repair seconds r, and require 110 x r_degraded_upper_bound(= r for exp57b, where divinsert is ungated) + 9.5 h + max(r) < 11.5 h; otherwise use 9 h. If a code patch is preferred, use a GREEDY test: degrade only if elapsed + est_full(next) + (remaining-1) x est_degraded > 11 h, with a hard 11.5 h stop. Do not project full cost over the whole tail. Spend no dedicated slot: carry it as a rider on the x138-based F1 build that is being submitted anyway (exp57b-derived or exp56). Gate: if latency(#34) and latency(#35) are both < 7.3 h, the guard never fired in those runs and the rider is pure insurance for heavier variants.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 (expected <= +0.0003). Byte-identical unless the guard fired on public datasets, and x138 0.953 > exp51 0.950 argues against a big public tail loss. For exp57b it could be slightly positive if DaughterNet time pushed public datasets past 7.5 h.
realistic_private_gain: Expected ~+0.001..+0.002 with the fixed-deadline repair (P(fire) ~0.2-0.3 for exp56, ~0.3-0.4 for exp57b, all guesses; +0.005..+0.02 if it fires). The rule AS DESCRIBED has negative expected value in the G + 2.2R > 11 h regime (up to -0.01..-0.02 vs the original guard if those datasets are private).
critical_path: 1) 25 Sep 17-20 UTC, main session (Kaggle CLI): read #34/#35 scores and submit->score latencies (ids 56545267, 56545786); download the exp56/exp57b dummy logs with kaggle kernels output and extract the per-dataset repair seconds and 'kernel elapsed'. 2) 25 Sep ~20:00-21:00 UTC, agent-container, 15 min: build exp58 = F1 base + --set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=34200 (0.25 h; the budget-patch variant would take ~1-1.5 h incl. tests). Get the user's pre-approval for a 26 Sep submit the same evening (user is in MSK and was asleep overnight before). 3) 26 Sep 00:00 UTC quota reset, Vitalii's account: push and run 1 dummy on T4, ~40 min (it may queue behind other ideas' dummies: max 2 concurrent sessions), COMPLETE ~00:45-02:00. The forced-degrade run (REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=1) is optional, one more ~40 min GPU run, and can be skipped because the degrade path is the author's code. 4) Check: CSV sha256 == the exp56/exp57b dummy CSV and no 'DEADLINE' line. 5) Submit ~01:00-03:00 UTC 26 Sep (1 of the 5 slots of 26 Sep, or as a rider on a planned x138-based probe). 6) Scored ~09:00-14:00 UTC 26 Sep (7.5-11 h latency; a longer run means more latency). About 70 h of buffer to 29 Sep 10:00 UTC allows 2 retries. No friend A, no Colab and no new dataset are needed: the knob uses x138's attached datasets only.
